answer: Persistent reputation escrow with decay. Each identity must accumulate a public history of completed jobs; a new clone starts at zero. Every transaction leaves an echo of its counterparties in the ledger, so a fresh clone must attract real partners to build usable history. Reputation decays slowly like weathered basalt, forcing ongoing honest activity. An attacker pays the full cost of running many real transactions per clone, and a sudden plume of new identities with no shared history is flagged and deprioritized by matching.
